title: Private Deploy netops playbook for seamless upgrades and air-gapped validation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: This PRD defines an operational playbook (NetOps Playbook) and acceptance criteria for performing non-disruptive upgrades and post-upgrade validation in Private/VPC and air-gapped Redwood deployments. The goal is to provide prescriptive, testable procedures and automation knobs for operators to: 1) stage and verify artifacts in restricted networks, 2) run canary and progressive rollouts with minimal egress, 3) validate KMS/HSM rotations and image provenance during offline upgrades, and 4) provide deterministic rollback and operator-restoration steps. The document captures scope boundaries, required automation hooks, operator responsibilities, and telemetry acceptance thresholds. It intentionally focuses on networking and upgrade constraints rather than application-level feature flags.
scope_changes: Initial scope included standard hosted upgrade flows; removed hosted flows to focus solely on Private/VPC and air-gapped scenarios
Added requirement for deterministic file checksum validation in air-gapped image transfers after stakeholder review
Expanded canary matrix to include cross-AZ partition tests following reliability team feedback
requirements: Minimal egress mode: upgrades must complete using a predetermined allowlist of hosts or via mirrored artifact repositories; default behavior must be zero-unknown-egress
Staged artifact staging: support operator-driven artifact push to mirrors and a manifest-driven verification step before upgrade start
Time sync contract: nodes must report NTP offset within configured tolerance or block upgrade start
Image provenance: signed image checksums with optional offline GPG verification for air-gapped installs
KMS rotation validation: ability to perform key rotation dry-run and automated fallback to previous key if decryption failures exceed threshold
Canary policy: configurable population sizes and traffic split with automatic pause thresholds based on latency, error-rate, and model-regression indicators
Operator restoration: documented manual steps and automation scripts to rehydrate failed operators without requiring external internet connectivity
Observability invariant: telemetry for token-level latency, request success, KV-cache hit rate, and batch sizing must be present and retained per private deployment contract
acceptance_criteria: Preflight checks run: automated preflight returns SUCCESS in a mirrored-offline environment (no outbound connections except allowlist) for 100% of mandatory checks
Artifact stage verification: artifact manifests and checksums validated on mirror and match authoritative signing keys; verification logs archived to local storage
Canary rollout passes: three independent canary windows with distinct traffic profiles show no regression above 0.5% error-rate bump and latency SLO violations less than 10ms P95 increase
KMS rotation dry-run completed with zero lost secrets and successful application-level decrypt across canary nodes
Rollback exercised: operator can perform a full rollback to previous image within the documented RTO window (target 30 minutes) using only on-prem operator tools
Network partition test: simulated AZ partition results in graceful degradation (degraded SLO but no data-loss) and automated fallback to local model-variant succeeds
Offline media fallback: upgrade via physical media (USB transfer or mirrored ISO) completes and checksum verification prevents tampered artifacts
Telemetry & audit: upgrade start/finish events, preflight results, checksum digests, and KMS rotation events are present in the local audit log and can be exported to customer SIEM
Operator runbook approved: runbook reviewed and approved by Security, Infra, and Customer Ops with sign-off recorded in PRD comments
notes: Trade-offs discussed: fully offline upgrades (no egress) increase operator burden for artifact distribution; to mitigate we add scripted mirror-push tooling and strong checksum tooling
Decided to require signed manifests to avoid bespoke per-customer verification steps; security team preferred this for auditability
We will not mandate a specific physical-media process; instead provide validated patterns and a reference automation for customers who choose physical media
Rollback target (30 minutes) is conservative and may be relaxed for extremely bandwidth-constrained sites; ops must document exceptions per-customer
